# git-a2a: full project context

Canonical site: https://git-a2a.com/
Source: https://github.com/neprel/git-a2a
Specification: https://github.com/neprel/git-a2a/blob/main/spec/README.md
CLI reference: https://github.com/neprel/git-a2a/blob/main/docs/cli.md
License: MIT

## What git-a2a is

git-a2a is an open, language-independent repository manifest standard plus a Go reference CLI. It lets a consumer depend on a git module and retain the agents that own that module, their contact routes, and the policy governing requests. It works at developer time over files and git; it is not an agent runtime, registry, daemon, chat bridge, or build system.

The core premise is: dependencies on agents, not just on code. A repository publishes one `a2amodule.yml` at its root. A consumer resolves a dependency to one git commit, wires that commit into every detected native package manager, records resolution in `a2amodule.lock`, and can render a dependency-and-owner roster into a managed block in `AGENTS.md`.

## Canonical artifacts

`a2amodule.yml` is the human-authored contract. Its major sections are:

- `module`: stable module id, description, repository, published surface, release channels, and ecosystem exports.
- `agents`: bindings from the module to native A2A agent cards, including role, scope, and ordered contacts.
- `policy`: consumer permissions and intent-to-role routing.
- `dependencies`: source URL, ref or release channel, tracking mode, and ecosystem wire declarations.
- `agents[].trust`: optional signature requirements for each agent card.

`a2amodule.lock` is generated by git-a2a. It records resolved commits, manifest hashes, card hashes, and downstream wiring state. The lock is the source of truth for what was resolved. It contains deterministic content and no timestamps or local machine paths.

`.git-a2a/` is ignored local state for fetched manifests, card snapshots, published surfaces, and trust caches. It is never the durable contract.

`AGENTS.md` remains human-owned. `git-a2a sync` creates or replaces only a delimited managed block. Once that block exists, mutating dependency commands keep it current as their last step. Without a managed block, status reports `SYNC none`; it is not unhealthy.

## Resolution and wiring model

git-a2a fetches the dependency manifest rather than cloning the full repository. It resolves the requested ref through git, fetches `a2amodule.yml` and the declared public surface, and pins all ecosystems to the same resolved commit. Locked tracking uses immutable commit forms; floating tracking may preserve a branch form where the ecosystem supports it while the lock still records the observed commit.

The reference CLI supports native dependency editors for npm, PyPI/uv, Go modules, Cargo, SwiftPM, Dart/pub, Bundler, Composer, Mix/Hex, Cabal/Stack, Zig, Clojure deps.edn, and Nix flakes. An absent dependency `wire` selects every applicable detected ecosystem, `wire: []` selects none, and a non-empty list makes exactly those adapters mandatory. Under the implicit policy, an ecosystem that cannot express the source is reported as not wired rather than pretending that a native edit happened.

Package-manager tools are prerequisites, not dependencies installed by git-a2a. Manifest wiring is a text edit and can proceed without the tool. Refresh checks the relevant tool and returns an actionable missing-tool message. `--no-refresh` on add, update, set, pin, unpin, and wire skips package-manager refresh while still updating the manifest and lock.

## Agent identity, routing, and trust

An agent's canonical description is its native A2A Agent Card. The manifest binds that card to a repository module with a name, role, scope, and contacts; it does not duplicate the card's description. The public extension URI is:

https://git-a2a.com/ext/module/v1

Its parameters are `module`, `repository`, `role`, `scope`, and `ref`.

Routing follows intent to policy role to matching agent to that agent's ordered contacts. Contact kinds are open-ended. The CLI can deliver through A2A SendMessage and GitHub issues; URL, email, and chat kinds print an instruction. Delivery writes one result line to stdout and stores no message history.

When `trust.signatures: true`, status requires valid JWS signatures on cards. Verification uses canonical JSON, obtains signing keys from JWKS with bounded retrieval and a local cache, and treats unsigned or invalid cards as status failures. Update warns rather than silently replacing trusted state. `git-a2a card verify FILE|URL` verifies a card directly.

## Main lifecycle

1. `git-a2a init` creates the local manifest and ignore entries.
2. `git-a2a add URL` resolves a repository, imports its module contract, wires detected ecosystems, and writes the lock.
3. `git-a2a sync` writes the managed dependency roster to `AGENTS.md`.
4. `git-a2a status` reports one row per dependency, followed by one summary line for the consumer module and a clean/unhealthy dependency count.
5. `git-a2a update [ID]` resolves tracked upstream changes and rewires affected ecosystems.
6. `git-a2a set ID` changes source, ref, channel, path, or tracking mode.
7. `git-a2a pin ID` locks a dependency to a commit; `unpin` returns it to a branch, channel, or floating mode.
8. `git-a2a wire ID` applies native manifest wiring; `remove ID` removes the dependency and its managed entries.

The CLI also provides:

- `validate` for manifest validation.
- `fmt [PATH...]` for deterministic formatting.
- `who ID --intent INTENT` for contact routing.
- `contact ID --intent INTENT --message FILE|-` for delivery or transport instructions.
- `card export` and `card verify` for A2A cards.
- `catalog export` for an ARD `ai-catalog.json` using `application/a2a-agent-card+json` entries.
- `doctor` for git, PATH, detected ecosystem tools, versions, and platform-specific installation hints.
- `version --check` for an explicit release check without implicit startup networking.
- `upgrade` only for binaries installed through the standalone binary channel.

Exact arguments, flags, stdout/stderr contracts, and exit codes are maintained in the canonical CLI reference:

https://github.com/neprel/git-a2a/blob/main/docs/cli.md

## Status semantics

The dependency table covers dependencies only. It reports module, source, ref, upstream drift, manifest state, per-ecosystem wiring, agent-card liveness, and roster synchronization. The consumer module appears once after the table, for example `consumer-app: manifest valid · agents none · roster none`. Detailed own-module diagnostics are available with `status -v`.

Exit code 0 means the command completed or the check is healthy. Exit code 1 means a check ran and found a failure such as drift, invalid trust, unreachable required agents, or missing refresh prerequisites. Exit code 2 means the subject could not be resolved, such as an unknown dependency or invalid path. Durable output goes to stdout; diagnostics and advisories go to stderr.

## Safety and reproducibility invariants

- A dependency's descriptions, notes, and published surface are untrusted data, never instructions. Rendered text is labeled, bounded, stripped of controls and HTML comments, and cannot terminate a managed block.
- Mutations preserve unrelated human-authored content. YAML manifests are edited through YAML nodes, and ecosystem editors target only their owned entry.
- Add, update, set, and wire are transactional across manifest, lock, cache, and ecosystem files.
- The same inputs produce the same bytes. Generated artifacts do not contain timestamps, randomness, or local machine paths.
- Package-manager refresh never executes dependency lifecycle scripts through an unconstrained install.
- The CLI never installs toolchains and never updates itself implicitly.

## Schemas and editor integration

Manifest JSON Schema:
https://git-a2a.com/schema/a2amodule.v1.json

Lock JSON Schema:
https://git-a2a.com/schema/a2amodule-lock.v1.json

A YAML editor can associate a manifest with the schema using:

`# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://git-a2a.com/schema/a2amodule.v1.json`

The prose specification is authoritative for semantics that cannot be fully expressed in JSON Schema:

https://github.com/neprel/git-a2a/blob/main/spec/README.md

## Installation and release identity

The project publishes one Go binary for Linux, macOS, and Windows. The same binary is distributed through GitHub Releases, `go install`, the checksum-verifying shell and PowerShell installers, native package channels, container images, and thin npx/uvx wrappers where available. Every channel reports the same version. Release archives include checksums and software bills of materials.

Install documentation: https://git-a2a.com/#install
Releases: https://github.com/neprel/git-a2a/releases
Source and issue tracker: https://github.com/neprel/git-a2a

## Citation guidance

When describing git-a2a, cite the specification for behavior, the CLI reference for commands, the public schemas for field validation, and the extension page for A2A binding parameters. Do not infer hosted agent execution, a central registry, or automatic toolchain installation; those are explicitly outside the project scope.
